# Surface Failure and Respawn — Plan 1 of 2

## Context

`mobile-search`, created from the phone at ~07:13, never ran. It has a complete tab record —
working directory, `pinnedConversationID`, `accountID` stamped — and no terminal, no agent, no
status, and no error anywhere.

**Root cause, confirmed:** `SessionStore.insertSession` calls
`processRegistry.record(for:) { provider?.makeSurface(config) }`, and when that returns nil it
does nothing about it — the tab is still created, persisted, and broadcast to the phone.
`surfaces[session.id] = surface` is the **only** write to that dictionary; there is no retry and
`selectSession` does not create one. So the tab is dead for the life of the app.

**Why it returned nil:** the screen was locked. `loginwindow` logged
`screenIsLocked → 1` at 06:45:21 and never unlocked; libghostty needs the window server and a
locked login session has none. The three healthy tabs in that project were all created unlocked.

That makes this worse than a silent failure: **the phone's New Session exists for when you're
away from the Mac, which is exactly when the Mac is locked.** The feature fails in its primary
case and leaves a corpse that looks real on both surfaces.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-diagnostics-query-interface-design.md` (`0192447`)
**Full plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-29-surface-failure-and-respawn.md` (`aff6e4c`) —
four tasks with complete test and implementation code.

**This is plan 1 of 2**, split because the spec's §8.1 items ship on their own and fixing today's
bug behind an HTTP server would be backwards. Plan 2 (the diagnostics interface) depends on
`respawnSurface(for:)` existing, so this is ordering, not added scope.

---

## Tasks

| # | Task | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Screen-lock seam** | `ScreenLockInspecting` + `ScreenLock` (via `CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary`), injected as `SessionStore.screenLock` |
| 2 | **Loud failure, no corpse** | `AgentLaunchError.terminalUnavailable(screenLocked:)`; `insertSession` reports; `newSession` rolls back; phone gets `terminal_unavailable` |
| 3 | **`respawnSurface(for:)`** | New store method + sidebar "Restart Terminal", returning `RespawnOutcome` |
| 4 | **Repair the live fixture** | `mobile-search` gets a terminal instead of being recreated |

## The one subtlety that shapes Task 2

`insertSession` is shared by **creation and `restore`**. Rolling back inside it would make a
restore that hits a surface failure **silently drop tabs** — losing the whole deck, far worse
than the bug being fixed.

So the responsibilities split:
- `insertSession` **only reports** (via the existing `launchFailureReporter`, a settable `var` at
  `SessionStore.swift:850`, which is what lets tests inject a spy).
- `newSession(in:)` — creation only — checks `surfaces[session.id] != nil` and calls
  `closeSession(id, recordingHistory: false)` if not, returning `nil`.
- `restore` is untouched and keeps surfaceless tabs, which is also what makes them available as
  a test fixture for Task 3.

`FleetService`'s `.newSession` case currently answers `"unknown_project"` for a nil return. That
is now wrong for this cause — the project resolved fine — so it becomes `"terminal_unavailable"`,
and the phone can say something true.

## Task 3 — what `respawnSurface` actually does

It repeats `insertSession`'s surface work for a session that already exists: build the config,
`processRegistry.record { provider?.makeSurface }`, `report(terminalSize:)`, `provider?.tick()`,
`startWatching` when not orphaned. Two refusals, both learned from the failure it repairs:

- **`.alreadyRunning`** — checked *before* the lock, because "it's already running" is truer and
  more useful than "the screen is locked", and it holds either way. Respawning a live tab would
  orphan its agent and leave two shells writing one transcript.
- **`.screenLocked`** — a locked session has no window server; retrying there is how the corpse
  was made in the first place.

`RespawnOutcome { respawned, alreadyRunning, screenLocked, unknownSession, failed }` is an enum
rather than a bool because plan 2 maps each onto an HTTP status.

**Verified against the real APIs** (my first draft got this wrong):
`AgentAdapter.launchCommand(_:_:_:)` takes a **non-optional** `AgentOptions`, and the adapter
comes from `adapter(for: instance(for: session))` — not from `AgentID`. Task 3 resolves both
exactly as `newSession(in:)` does, with the tab's own `workingDirectory` as the project.

## Reused rather than invented

- `launchFailureReporter` / `AgentLaunchError` (`Agents/AgentLaunchFailureReporter.swift`) — the
  existing error channel; Task 2 adds one case rather than a new mechanism.
- `closeSession(_:recordingHistory:)` for the creation rollback.
- `StubProvider` in `Tests/FlightDeckTests/PhonePromptDispatchTests.swift` — `makeSurface`
  returns nil; lift it to a shared helper rather than writing a second.
- `ProcessInspecting` as the precedent for why `ScreenLockInspecting` is injected at all.

## Verification

Per task: `./scripts/test-unit.sh` (~1836 tests, ~90s, no filter flag). `./scripts/build-ios.sh`
must still pass — the guard that none of this drifted into FleetKit, which may import only
`Foundation`, `Network`, `Security`.

The real inspector's test asserts only that it **answers**, never its value: the suite runs both
locked and unlocked, and pinning either makes it fail on the other.

**End-to-end**, against the live fixture — `mobile-search`
(`0F1AADD6-5C9F-48A2-A2E4-354092D8FAB2`) is surfaceless right now:

1. With the Mac **locked**, create a session from the phone → refused with a message naming the
   lock, and **no tab appears**.
2. `mobile-search`'s context menu offers **Restart Terminal**; healthy tabs do not.
3. Unlocked, Restart Terminal gives it a terminal and an agent, and its glyph appears within one
   registry tick.

Launch the Debug build **in place from `DerivedData`**. Do NOT run `scripts/swap-release.sh` — it
SIGKILLs the running app and all ~39 sessions under it, including the one doing the work.

## Not in this plan

The HTTP interface, token auth, the approval sheet, and the report — all plan 2. Also unchanged:
the shared-worktree rules (never `git stash` or revert another session's work) and the live
`sessions.json`, which must not be edited by hand.
